column1: # precision_overrides.tsv — shared implementations the matrix's name-based rule cannot see.
# tools/precision_matrix.sh decides "dtype X has capability C" from the dtype token in a symbol's name
# (falling back to the module folder it lives in). That is correct wherever the dtype IS in the name, and
# structurally blind in two cases, both of which live here:
#   1. one precision REUSES another's implementation — fp16 multicore IS i8/colsplit.c, and no single name
#      can say "serves i8 and f16" without lying about one of them;
#   2. the symbol is dtype-tagged but the capability regex does not reach it.
# Each row renders as a dagger + footnote, so a reused implementation reads "supported, via X" not a gap.
# THE SYMBOL FIELD IS LOAD-BEARING: check_registry.sh check 8 fails the build if a cited symbol stops
# being defined, so a dagger can never outlive the code it points at. Cite the function that actually does
# the work for the borrowing dtype — the shared core, not the caller.
# This gate earned its keep on its first run: it killed a "run — multicore / i16 / routed through the int8
# chain" row that had NO symbol behind it, because there is no i16 multicore path at all (the only i16 x
# multicore thing in the tree is ORK_OP_MATMUL_I16OUT_I8 — an int8 matmul that EMITS int16, which is the
# int8 row, not an i16 one). Hand-written matrix claims rot in exactly this direction.
# capability<TAB>dtype<TAB>symbol<TAB>why
